evidence.title: Identificar qué se calibra
evidence.body:
Distinguir calibración del pulso RF, escala de gradiente y referencia térmica.
El valor de un cero por sí solo no identifica el ángulo. Después, un gradiente con error de escala produce un error cuadrático en b y en la D ajustada frente al eje nominal.
Mantén potencia, fase y condiciones constantes durante la nutación. Utiliza el máximo anterior y el cambio de polaridad para identificar el primer cruce a 180°; entonces P90=P180/2. Si el cero corresponde a 360°, la división correcta es entre cuatro. El número de experimento sólo identifica el registro. Para el gradiente, usa un patrón con D de referencia apropiada a la temperatura y matriz, la misma secuencia y la forma completa de gradiente. Si g_real=s g_nominal, entonces D_nominal=s² D_referencia y s=sqrt(D_nominal/D_referencia). Una temperatura guardada en acqus no demuestra calibración térmica independiente.
Equation: P90=P180/2=P360/4; b_actual=s^2 b_nominal; s=sqrt(D_nominal/D_reference)
Units: Pulse duration: us; g: T/m; temperature: K; D: m2/s
Assumptions: Constant RF power and phase during the pulse-duration sweep.; The entire effective gradient waveform scales by s.; A standard, matrix, temperature and sequence-specific b expression must be appropriate.

evidence.title: Incertidumbre compartida y ruido independiente
evidence.body:
Separar ruido, calibración, temperatura, procesado y supuestos de modelo.
La calibración afecta conjuntamente a todos los gradientes y frecuencias. Muestrear un factor independiente en cada punto representaría otra experiencia y subestimaría o distorsionaría el error compartido.
En cada realización Monte Carlo se sortea una sola escala de gradiente para toda la rampa y los canales que comparten calibración. Se distinguen las variables comunes, como temperatura o referencia, del ruido independiente. Se vuelve a ejecutar el análisis con los parámetros muestreados y se informa qué fuentes domina cada intervalo. Repetir adquisiciones puede reducir la dispersión de ruido, pero no elimina un sesgo común. Un bootstrap de residuos condicionado a b fijo no incluye automáticamente incertidumbre de calibración, temperatura, baseline, correlación espectral o elección de secuencia. El intervalo del modelo es condicional: su cobertura requiere pruebas independientes, primero con simulaciones de verdad conocida.
Equation: g_j^(r)=s^(r) g_j, for all j in one realization; b_j^(r)=(s^(r))^2 b_j; DeltaD/D approximately 2 Deltas/s for small scale errors
Units: Scale factors: dimensionless; temperature: K; D intervals: m2/s
Assumptions: The stated uncertainty distributions and correlations are modelling assumptions.; Model discrepancy is not automatically represented by a narrow bootstrap interval.; Reported synthetic coverage is not experimental coverage.

evidence.title: Processing as a reproducible decision
evidence.body:
Preserve the FID and assess sensitivity to explicit processing choices.
Attenuation is estimated from processed signals. A narrow window, incorrect phase or row-dependent baseline can turn a processing problem into an apparent D.
Inspect complex FID organization, the digital filter, time units and frequency reference. Record apodization, zero filling, phase, baseline and integration. Zero filling interpolates the display and does not create acquired resolution. Retain signed integrals: taking absolute values or unjustifiably discarding rows changes information and can bias the curve. A log fit requires positive intensities; a direct fit must state its noise model and parameters. Compare integration windows and phase decisions using the same FID, and export both parameters and provenance. The public D2O dataset retains its nominal/conditional b and D scale.

Units: Frequency: ppm or Hz with stated reference; time: s; D: m2/s

evidence.title: Shared uncertainty and independent noise
evidence.body:
Separate noise, calibration, temperature, processing and model assumptions.
Calibration affects every gradient and frequency jointly. Drawing an independent factor for every point would represent a different experiment and underestimate or distort the shared error.
Each Monte Carlo realization draws one gradient scale for the whole ramp and all channels sharing that calibration. Common variables such as temperature or reference are distinguished from independent noise. The analysis is rerun with sampled parameters, and the dominant sources are reported. Repeated acquisitions may reduce noise scatter but do not remove a common bias. A residual bootstrap conditional on fixed b does not automatically include uncertainty in calibration, temperature, baseline, spectral correlation or sequence choice. A model interval is conditional: its coverage requires independent checks, initially using simulations with known truth.

Para el gradiente, usa un patrón con D de referencia apropiada a la temperatura y matriz, la misma secuencia y la forma completa de gradiente. Si g_real=s g_nominal, entonces D_nominal=s² D_referencia y s=sqrt(D_nominal/D_referencia). Una temperatura guardada en acqus no demuestra calibración térmica independiente.
Equation: P90=P180/2=P360/4; b_actual=s^2 b_nominal; s=sqrt(D_nominal/D_reference)
Units: Pulse duration: us; g: T/m; temperature: K; D: m2/s

evidence.title: Shared uncertainty and independent noise
evidence.body:
Separate noise, calibration, temperature, processing and model assumptions.
Calibration affects every gradient and frequency jointly. Drawing an independent factor for every point would represent a different experiment and underestimate or distort the shared error.
Each Monte Carlo realization draws one gradient scale for the whole ramp and all channels sharing that calibration. Common variables such as temperature or reference are distinguished from independent noise. The analysis is rerun with sampled parameters, and the dominant sources are reported. Repeated acquisitions may reduce noise scatter but do not remove a common bias. A residual bootstrap conditional on fixed b does not automatically include uncertainty in calibration, temperature, baseline, spectral correlation or sequence choice. A model interval is conditional: its coverage requires independent checks, initially using simulations with known truth.
Equation: g_j^(r)=s^(r) g_j, for all j in one realization; b_j^(r)=(s^(r))^2 b_j; DeltaD/D approximately 2 Deltas/s for small scale errors
Units: Scale factors: dimensionless; temperature: K; D intervals: m2/s
Assumptions: The stated uncertainty distributions and correlations are modelling assumptions.; Model discrepancy is not automatically represented by a narrow bootstrap interval.; Reported synthetic coverage is not experimental coverage.
